channel.title: The Colorado Sun - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Colorado Sun (coloradosun.com)

item.title: Wildfire south of Colorado Springs grows to 7,300 acres as crews gain some containment
item.description: Fire crews were able to start “boxing in” the 24 fire overnight but state highway will remain closed through this week

item.title: Opinion: Colorado bill that would extend infant abandonment window is misguided
item.description: House Bill 1024 is a solution looking for a problem and undermines best practices in adoption.

item.title: Shannon Bird’s “no” votes on some big Democratic bills may both help and hurt her run for Congress
item.description: The former state representative is taking heat in the 8th Congressional District Democratic primary for her votes on immigration bills and funding questions

item.title: As the BLM in Moab opens hundreds of miles of trails to e-bikes, Colorado land managers also weigh expansion
item.description: The BLM’s Colorado River Valley Field Office is reviewing a plan to open 220 miles of trails to e-bikes in Eagle, Pitkin, Garfield counties

item.title: Colorado lawmakers step in — again — to urge federal action on stalled tribal water access
item.description: The Southern Ute and Ute Mountain Ute officials have pushed for federal action on water projects for years. Colorado lawmakers join in the fight.

item.title: Opinion: Will more of the Colorado River flow uphill toward the Front Range money?
item.description: As water battle heats up across the Southwest, the next year will be the most fascinating, and litigious, in the history of the Colorado River.

item.title: "What'd I Miss?": When "fascism" fits
item.description: Ossie and his friend explore the meaning of facism — and wonder why they don't hear the term invoked more in discussions of American history.

item.title: Drew Litton: Easter basket of economic misery
item.description: The cartoonist illustrates everyone's frustration — even the Easter bunny — with an economy that offers little relief from rising prices.

item.title: Silverman: How human error built some of Colorado’s greatest sports moments
item.description: New technology is embarrassing sports officials, but history shows Colorado teams benefiting from bad calls

item.title: Are Denver police prohibited from chasing motorcyclists?
item.description: No. Though Denver police must follow all pursuit regulations under department policy, there is no specific ban on pursuing motorcycles.

item.title: Colorado Springs snowboarder Noah Elliott carves path to gold at Milano Cortina Paralympics
item.description: The five-time world champion and two-time Paralympian trained with the elite Steamboat Adaptive Recreational Sports team

item.title: Even if Coloradans slash their water use, their bills will likely rise during drought
item.description: Drought fees on the horizon for major communities such as Denver and Aurora, as utilities forecast financial losses due to lower water sales

item.title: A dose of amino acids could give developing Western Slope peaches strength to survive deadly spring freezes
item.description: Colorado State University researchers are set to test their theory against a freeze forecast for this weekend

item.title: It’s been the worst year for Colorado’s snowpack in recorded history. A striking new map shows why.
item.description: Colorado's snowpack is at historic lows on the eave of runoff season, and a shocking heat map for March 2026 shows why.

item.title: Half of staff at Boulder’s NOAA Global Monitoring Lab face furloughs as funding freeze drags on
item.description: About half of the staff at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s Global Monitoring Lab in Boulder could be furloughed in May.
